name: Tukangbesi Sunbird
rangeDescription: Wakatobi (tukangbesi) islands (off southeastern sulawesi)
description: Tiny and active sunbird of forest edges and open woodlands. Endemic to the Tukangbesi archipelago, off southeastern Sulawesi.

name: Dusky Babbler
rangeDescription: Northeastern central african republic to northwestern uganda and southwestern ethiopia
description: A very dark babbler with a pale eye. Found very locally in areas of moist woodland with thick undergrowth, almost always in small groups that feed by hopping across the ground.

name: Cook's Petrel
rangeDescription: Breeds islands off new zealand; ranges to eastern and north pacific
description: A small, fast-flying petrel with long narrow wings and bright white underparts. Found singly or in loose aggregations, well offshore in warmer Pacific waters, mainly from March to August.

name: Ring-tailed Pigeon
rangeDescription: Jamaica
description: A large pale pigeon primarily of montane and foothill forests; often occurs in small flocks and found high in trees. The banded tail is unique among pigeons in its range.

name: Imperial Eagle
rangeDescription: Central europe to mongolia; winters to africa, northern india, and china
description: Very large; dark-brown body of adult contrasts with pale head and nape. Similar to Golden Eagle but with a shorter tail and white shoulders that can be hard to spot.

name: Malayan Cuckooshrike
rangeDescription: Peninsular malaysia
description: A large gray cuckooshrike endemic to the hill and montane forests of peninsular Malaysia. Gray above with black primaries; also note strong, slightly hooked bill.

name: Dwarf Bittern
rangeDescription: Sub-saharan africa
description: Tiny, compact, dark bittern. Slate-gray on the upperparts and pale on the underparts, which have thick dark streaks.

name: Stuhlmann's Starling
rangeDescription: Patchily distributed in southwestern ethiopia, southern south sudan (imatong mountains), eastern democratic republic of the congo, western uganda, rwanda, burundi, and western tanzania
description: Small, slim dark starling. The eyes are brown, and females show large chestnut patches in the wings in flight.
imageCreditName: Lars Petersson | My World of Bird Photography

name: White-eyed Gull
rangeDescription: Red sea and gulf of aqaba to gulf of aden
description: A unique medium-sized, lightly-built gull, confined to the Red Sea. Upperparts dark brown or gray.

name: Para Foliage-gleaner
rangeDescription: Brazil south of the amazon river (rio madeira to rio tocantins)
description: Medium-sized and typically noisy foliage-gleaner with an olive-brown back, buff underparts, a white throat, and a rusty tail. Found mainly in humid lowland forest, often near streams, but also sometimes in seasonally flooded forests.

name: Fiordland Penguin
rangeDescription: South island (new zealand) and adjacent subantarctic islands
description: Tall penguin endemic to New Zealand, with distinct broad yellow eyebrow that spreads out and sags down the neck. The orange bill has no bare skin at the base.

name: Stub-tailed Antbird
rangeDescription: Pacific slope of western colombia and northwestern ecuador (esmeraldas)
description: Fairly small, chunky, and short-tailed antbird. Male is jet black.

name: Bernier's Vanga
rangeDescription: Humid forest of eastern madagascar
description: Large, slim, dark, long-billed vanga. Males are glossy black, females are rich brown with dark bars, and both sexes show a piercing pale eye.

name: Scopoli's Shearwater
rangeDescription: Breeds mediterranean islands, outside breeding season moving to winter mainly in upwelling systems of tropical eastern atlantic
description: Large, lumbering shearwater. Diagnostic yellow bill is often visible from quite a long distance.

name: Slender-billed Finch
rangeDescription: Coastal western peru (lima) to andes of northern chile
description: Long-tailed, often rather skulking “finch” (actually a tanager) of scrub, hedges, and riverside thickets in desert lowlands, where no very similar species are found. Adult blue-gray overall with slender, bright yellow bill, and yellow legs; tail often held cocked.

name: Cory's Shearwater
rangeDescription: Eastern atlantic, breeding from azores southward to canary islands and eastward to galicia (northwestern spain) and berlengas islands (off west-central portugal); outside breeding season ranges widely in atlantic, but mainly in upwelling systems of the benguela and agulhas currents
description: Large, lumbering shearwater. Diagnostic yellow bill is often visible from quite a long distance.

name: Spotted Fantail
rangeDescription: Southern peninsular thailand, malaya, sumatra, and borneo
description: A starburst of vanilla sprinkles across the breast makes this black-and-white fantail unmistakable. Irrepressibly hyperactive, it is often an active member of mixed-species foraging flocks in the middle and upper levels of forest.

name: Red-naped Sapsucker
rangeDescription: Southwestern canada to southwestern usa; winters to northern mexico and southern baja california
description: Striking medium-sized woodpecker of western North America. Long, solid white wing patch helps distinguish it from Downy and Hairy Woodpeckers.

name: White-breasted Mesite
rangeDescription: Dry deciduous forest of western madagascar
description: Odd ground-dwelling bird that is rarely seen by those not looking for it. Brown upperparts, pale underparts, and elaborately striped head.

name: Buffy Laughingthrush
rangeDescription: Mountains of southeastern china (northwestern yunnan, gansu, and southern sichuan eastward to anhui, zhejiang and northwestern fujian)
description: Bright rufous laughingthrush with a gray belly and bright blue facial skin patch. Restricted to primary montane forest but will occasionally move downslope in winter.
